items.title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 shuttle buses for Malaysian GP at Sepang
items.summary: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service was aimed at meeting the transport needs of motorsports fans and facilitating their journeys to the circuit. He said tickets would go on sale from October 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub. Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from three main locations, namely the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.

items.title: Anwar congratulates Zuhairie on Malaysia's first gold at Asian Para Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi for winning Malaysia's first gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Anwar said the achievement was even sweeter as Zuhairie had also broken the Games record during the qualifying round. "Congratulations and well done, Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia's key index ends below 1,600 support level, baking stocks weigh
items.summary: For banking counters, Public Bank erased 12 sen to RM4.71, Maybank shed nine sen to RM9.90, CIMB eased five sen to RM7.15, AMMB Holdings slipped 16 sen to RM6.19, and RHB Bank went down 12 sen to RM7.20. Among other heavyweights, Press Metal jumped 18 sen to RM6.68, YTL Power advanced 11 sen to RM5.26, SD Guthrie improved three sen to RM5.72, while TNB gave up two sen to RM12.98 and IHH Healthcare shaved off 10 sen to RM7.90. Of the active stocks, Ni Hsin put on 2.5 sen to 44.5 sen, V.S Industry and MAG Holdings were flat at 34 sen and 15.5 sen, respectively, Zetrix AI and JAKS Resources edged down half-a-sen each to five sen and 14 sen, respectively, and Top Glove slid one sen to 89 sen.

items.title: Anwar congratulates para cyclist Zuhairie on winning Malaysia’s first gold at 2026 Asian Para Games
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi for winning Malaysia’s first gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. “Congratulations and well done, Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi. Zuhairie secured Malaysia’s first gold medal at the Games after winning the men’s C4-C5 (physical impairment) 1,000-metre (m) time trial final at the Izu Velodrome earlier today.

items.title: Haze: Johan Setia, Batu Muda among 25 areas with unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 25 areas recorded unhealthy air quality as of 5pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 168. Another 39 locations recorded moderate API readings, including areas in Johor, Pahang, Selangor and Sarawak. An API reading of 101 to 200 is classified as unhealthy, while readings between 51 and 100 indicate moderate air quality.

items.title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 buses for MotoGP shuttle service
items.summary: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service aimed to meet motorsports fans' transport needs and make their journeys to the circuit more convenient. He said tickets would go on sale on Oct 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub. Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from 3 locations: the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.

items.title: Haze: 27 areas in Malaysia record unhealthy air quality as of 4pm, Johan Setia in Selangor records highest reading of 169
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A total of 27 areas nationwide continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading of 169. Six areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tangkak (161), Pasir Gudang (157), Batu Pahat (156), Larkin (140), Kota Tinggi (128) and Kluang (105). A total of 38 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three areas - Labuan (48), Kimanis in Sabah (43) and Limbang in Sarawak (35) - recorded good readings.

items.title: Khee San in MoU with Paul Lim, sundry goods merchants, to develop digitalization platform for retailers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Khee San Bhd has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Federation of Sundry Goods Merchants Associations of Malaysia and business owner Dr Paul Lim Pang Kiam to develop a digitalisation platform for independent sundry goods retailers. The platform aims to help retailers adopt digital tools, prepare for e-Invoice requirements and improve operational efficiency and purchasing power. Khee San managing director Desmond Yong Loong Chen said the initiative would bring practical digital solutions to independent sundry goods retailers, including tools to improve daily operations and facilitate collective purchasing.

items.title: Mi Technovation semiconductor material unit launches SGX listing at S$1.80 per share
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Material Holding Ltd, a unit of Mi Technovation Bhd, had launched its initial public offering (IPO) on the Singapore Exchange, pricing its shares at S$1.80 each, to raise a total of S$203.2 million (RM829.58 million). The listing comprises a total offering of 77.5 million shares. This involves a fresh issuance of 51.5 million new shares by Mi Material, alongside 26 million existing shares offered by Mi Technovation as the vendor.

items.title: Retain SST and improve it instead of reviving GST, says Bangi MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should retain the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) system and improve it where necessary instead of reinstating the Goods and Services Tax (GST), Bangi member of parliament Syahredzan Johan said. Syahredzan said reintroducing the GST would require more than 900,000 businesses to register and collect the tax, compared with about 132,000 under the current SST system. Syahredzan also said the GST would burden small businesses, which would have to manage tax refunds and other related administrative matters.

items.title: Lorry driver injured after tipper overturns in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 40-year-old lorry driver was injured when his 10-tonne tipper lorry carrying rocks skidded and overturned along Jalan Pulau Lumut. The driver was trapped inside the vehicle. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said firefighters received an emergency call at 3.03pm.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Pahang to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
items.summary: In Melaka, the State Education Department said that students attending school were encouraged to wear face masks, while parents or guardians who were concerned about their children’s health were allowed to keep them at home, provided that they informed the school. In Selangor, the State Education Department also said that schools would operate as usual, but outdoor activities had been postponed, with students attending school encouraged to wear face masks. In Negeri Sembilan, the State Education Department said that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) across the state would also operate as usual tomorrow.

items.title: Australian lawmaker 'critically' hurt in attack, officials say
items.summary: Haines was hurt outside her office in Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northwest of Melbourne, police said. The 65-year-old "suffered what has been described as critical injuries", Victoria Police Acting Superintendent Ashley Mason said, without identifying the victim in line with police custom in Australia. The alleged attacker's motive remained unknown, Albanese said, with Australia's counter-terrorism squad activated.

items.title: 1MDB gets fresh hearing on US$3.78bil judgment against Jho Low, father
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today ordered the High Court to rehear an application by 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and four of its subsidiaries to set aside a judgment in default (JID) entered against fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho and his father, Tan Sri Larry Low Hock Peng. Azhahari ordered the case to be remitted to the High Court for a full hearing before a different judge and fixed Oct 26 for case management at the High Court. Last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court dismissed the companies' application to set aside the JID on the grounds that they had delayed filing it by nearly three years.

items.title: Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan schools stay open tomorrow: Outdoor activities halt
items.summary: In Selangor, the state education department said schools would also operate as usual, but outdoor activities had been postponed. Students were encouraged to wear face masks. In Negri Sembilan, the state education department said all educational institutions under the Education Ministry across the state would operate as usual tomorrow.

items.title: MyEG probe into RM230.9m govt revenue case widens, 15 questioned, including 12 JPJ officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The police have recorded statements from 15 individuals to assist in investigations into allegations of failure to transfer RM230.9 million in government revenue, involving MyEG Sdn Bhd (MyEG) and Zetrix AI Berhad. Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said those questioned comprised 12 Road Transport Department (JPJ) officers and three bank officers. “So far, statements have been recorded from 15 individuals, comprising 12 from JPJ and three bank officers,” he said today.

items.title: Man remanded four days for threatening, chasing wife with parang
items.summary: Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman issued the remand order against the 42-year-old suspect, effective today, to facilitate investigations. The incident reportedly occurred at a house in Sungai Kalong, Senggarang, at 8.30am yesterday. Police said initial investigations found that the suspect had taken a 62cm parang and chased his 37-year-old wife while making threats that frightened her.

items.title: Singapore issues haze notices to three more Indonesian companies
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore will issue preventive measure notices (PMNs) to three more Indonesian companies suspected of links to fires in Kalimantan that may have contributed to transboundary haze. The National Environment Agency (NEA) today identified the three additional companies as PT Buana Megatama Jaya, PT Mananjung Hayak, and PT Baratama Putra Perkasa. The seven companies issued notices on Friday were PT Bumi Andalas Permai, PT Bumi Mekar Hijau, PT Paramitra Mulia Langgeng, PT Sumatera Alam Anugerah, PT SBA Wood Industries, PT Hutan Lestari Raya, and PT Bangkanesia.

items.title: [UPDATED] Teresa Kok wins defamation suit against Akmal, awarded RM250,000
items.summary: MELAKA: DAP veteran Teresa Kok has won her defamation suit against Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Salleh, with the High Court awarding her RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages. Kok's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said in a statement that judge Isa Aziz Ibrahim had also granted an injunction restraining the Umno Youth chief from making further defamatory statements against her. The court also ordered the removal of the impugned statements from all social media platforms, he said.

items.title: Data Centre Bill to be presented to cabinet next year, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy while addressing utility constraints and avoiding disproportionate environmental impacts. He said the agreement followed a presentation by the Digital Ministry on the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development. Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries and the implementing agencies would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Economy Ministry.

items.title: Three houses damaged after trees fall in Bayan Lepas
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Three houses were damaged after three trees fell on their roofs at Kampung Bukit, Bayan Lepas, today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.56pm. "We found the three trees on the roofs of three houses, partially damaging the structures.

items.title: Businessman loses appeal to claim RM185,671 lottery prize without ticket in Shah Alam court
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — A businessman has failed in his bid to recover RM185,671 from Pan Malaysian Pools Sdn Bhd after losing his winning lottery ticket. At the Shah Alam High Court today, judicial commissioner Seow Hock Peng dismissed M Mahendravarman’s appeal against a Sessions Court ruling that rejected his claim against the lottery operator, Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported. The company refused to pay without the original ticket.

items.title: Police record statements from 15 in RM230.9mil MyEG, Zetrix AI probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded statements from 15 people to assist investigations into the alleged failure to remit RM230.9 million in government revenue collections involving electronic service providers MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd. Federal Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said in a statement that those questioned comprised 12 Road Transport Department (RTD) officers and three bank officers. Zetrix AI, formerly known as MYEG Services Bhd, has provided online government services, including those linked to RTD, since 2000.

items.title: Bangi MP calls for fair allocations regardless of political affiliation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should enact legislation to guarantee constituency allocations for all members of parliament (MPs), regardless of political affiliation, Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan said. He said the amount allocated should be determined using a proportional formula to ensure fair distribution. DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo had also called on the government to enact legislation guaranteeing fair allocations to all MPs without political discrimination.

items.title: Record El Nino? Depends who's counting
items.summary: BRITAIN'S Met Office says this year's El Nino is "unprecedented." The answer lies in how they measure El Nino's strength, with meteorological agencies using different methods to assess the climate phenomenon that make direct comparisons difficult. The Pacific Ocean's El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the planet's main natural climate driver.

items.title: Speaker tells MPs to exercise caution when using religious terms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Members of Parliament have been reminded to exercise caution when using religious terms that could lead to misunderstandings and prolonged disputes in the Dewan Rakyat. "I did not attend a religious school. Johari said MPs should be mindful of the differing levels of understanding among their fellow MPs when using religious terminology.

items.title: Three women arrested over fake medical certificates in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Three women were arrested here yesterday afternoon to assist in investigations involving fake medical certificates (MCs) used to deceive employers in the district. District Police Chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the three women, aged between 22 and 23, were detained at 3.20pm. "Police believe the arrests will assist investigations into several cases involving forged medical leave documents around the Kota Tinggi district.

items.title: RM500 monthly aid to support Norhazwani's two daughters
items.summary: TUMPAT: The sister of Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, who was killed last week, is expected to receive RM500 in monthly assistance to help care for the victim's two young daughters. Kelantan Social Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the aid would be provided under the Foster Child Assistance scheme, which allocates RM250 per child each month. However, he said the assistance could only be disbursed to Marliza Ibrahim, 48, after the court officially granted custody of the children to the victim's family.

items.title: Religious scholars must keep up with advances in science and technology, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Religious scholars need to broaden their knowledge by keeping abreast of developments in science, technology and geopolitics to ensure that the message of dakwah remains relevant in addressing contemporary global challenges. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said mastery of contemporary knowledge must go hand in hand with the study of traditional Islamic knowledge and ‘turath’ (Islamic classical heritage) to enable religious scholars to understand global changes and address the challenges facing the ummah more comprehensively. Zulkifli said global technological and geopolitical developments required society, including religious scholars, to understand strategic issues and avoid becoming preoccupied with trivial matters and differences of opinion that offered little benefit.

items.title: Australian teens disclose online sexual harm to AI chatbots
items.summary: CANBERRA: Australian teenagers who experience online sexual abuse are more likely to disclose it to artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots than to authorities, a national study has found, reported Xinhua. The study of almost 2,000 Australians aged 16 to 18, conducted in early 2026 by Adelaide University's Australian Cybercrime Observatory, found that 18.7 per cent of victims told an AI about their experience. Girls experienced higher rates of online sexual victimisation overall, but boys were significantly more likely to be targeted when AI was involved, it said.

items.title: Two men fined RM6,000 each for stealing telecommunications components
items.summary: Mohd Syahrul Mohamed Sarip, 40, and Mohd Fahmi Mat, 31, entered their pleas after the charges were read out before magistrate Nik Mohd Tarmizie Nik Mohd Shukri. Nik Mohd Tarmizie fined both men RM6,000 each. For this charge, Nik Mohd Tarmizie fined Syahrul RM7,000.

items.title: Poultry farm operator slapped with RM50,000 fine for fly breeding offence
items.summary: PARIT BUNTAR, Oct 19 — A poultry farm operator was fined RM50,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of allowing fly breeding at two poultry farm premises in Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, last July. According to the first charge, Siah was accused of allowing fly breeding at a PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm at Lot 5020, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 9.40 am on July 16. He was also charged with committing the same offence at another PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm along Jalan Changkat Lobak, Beriah, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 12.16 pm on the same day.

items.title: Lawyer says eviction bid halted, court order to be sought for Balai Undang Rembau
items.summary: REMBAU, Oct 19 — The Balai Undang Luak Rembau today faced another attempt at eviction when several senior government officials arrived to reclaim possession of the premises. Online . Lawyer representing the Balai Undang Luak Rembau, Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, said those present included the director of the Land and Mines Office (PTG), the Rembau district officer, the district police chief and several other department heads.

items.title: Bus Cap appoints Ma Xiyin as independent, non-executive director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bus Cap Bhd, Malaysia's first pure-play bus builder listed on Bursa Malaysia, has appointed Ma Xiyin as an independent non-executive director, effective Oct 16. The appointment strengthens the board's expertise in new-energy technologies and electric mobility as the group expands beyond conventional bus manufacturing, the group said in a statement. Her experience across China's new-energy and electric mobility industries brings valuable perspectives at an important stage of our group's development," said Bus Cap executive director Bernard Ng Chong Yan.

items.title: Housewife loses nearly RM88,000 in fake online investment scam
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 63-year-old housewife lost RM87,975.04 after being duped by a non-existent online investment scheme. Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim came across a stock investment advertisement on Facebook on Oct 3. "The suspect persuaded the victim to join the scheme by promising lucrative returns of RM25,000 for every RM450 invested.

items.title: BKE traffic diversion near Lunas on Oct 21 for emergency drill
items.summary: Plus Malaysia Berhad (Plus) said in a statement today that the diversion would be in effect from 10.30am to 12.30pm to facilitate an emergency simulation exercise. "The exercise will test the efficiency, response times, preparedness and actions of PLUS, rescue teams and relevant agencies when dealing with highway emergencies. The exercise will involve Plus personnel and various agencies, including the Malaysian Highway Authority, police and fire and rescue department.

items.title: Calls grow to bring Malaysian elephants home
items.summary: The three elephants, named Dara, Amoi and Kelat, were transferred to the zoo in March. Pertubuhan Konservasi Alam Malaysia activist Dr Siti Rabiah Raws said the elephants had been observed displaying repetitive stereotypical behaviour, including excessive head swaying. Siti Rabiah said Kelat's frequent musth cycles required urgent attention.

items.title: China set to leave benchmark lending rates unchanged for 17th month
items.summary: SHANGHAI: China is set to leave benchmark lending rates unchanged for a 17th consecutive month in October, a Reuters survey showed, after better-than-expected third-quarter GDP data lessened prospects for near-term easing. The loan prime ‌rate (LPR), normally charged to banks' most creditworthy clients, is calculated each month after 20 designated commercial banks submit proposed rates to the People's Bank of China (PBOC). The overwhelming consensus for steady LPR settings comes as some major economies tilt towards tighter monetary policy to contain inflation pressures, while China's long-dated bond yields hovered near a 15-month low.

items.title: KL JPJ records RM376,091 in proceeds from seized vehicle auction
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (JPJ) generated RM376,091 from its Public Auction of Seized Vehicles (Series 2/2026), conducted through the JPJvBID system. Its director, Hamidi Adam, said 120 of the 157 vehicles offered were successfully auctioned, surpassing the results of the previous auction series. Hamidi said the results reflected the effectiveness of the JPJvBID system as a transparent, efficient and accessible digital auction platform.

items.title: Sarawak set to become Borneo's international arbitration hub
items.summary: KUCHING: Sarawak is set to become a regional hub for international arbitration in Borneo with the establishment of an office of the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) in the state, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. She said the office was also expected to spur international business and trade activities in Borneo. "The facility will provide opportunities for legal practitioners in Sarawak and Sabah to explore international arbitration, which operates according to international standards, particularly as Sarawak is experiencing rapid growth in business and international trade.

items.title: Traffic diversion on Butterworth-Kulim Expressway for two hours from 10.30am on Oct 21
items.summary: During the exercise, affected motorists will be diverted through the eastbound Penanti Rest and Service Area (R&R). The exercise aims to assess PLUS and the relevant agencies’ preparedness, response time and coordination in handling highway emergencies, as well as evaluate accident response and safety procedures. Participating agencies include PLUS, the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Health Ministry (KKM), Department of Environment (DOE), Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM), transport strategic partner Prifaria Sdn Bhd and highway maintenance contractor Edgenta Infrastructure Services (EIS).

items.title: Malaysia advocating Asean self-reliance in essential medicines, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia is spearheading efforts to strengthen Asean’s self-reliance in essential medicines and reduce dependence on vulnerable global supply chains as part of a broader push to enhance regional health security, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. “Health security demands stronger regional capacity to secure essential medicines, rather than reliance on fragile external supply chains,” he said when delivering Malaysia’s country statement at the 77th Regional Committee Meeting for the Western Pacific in Manila, the Philippines, here today. Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening regional health security is reflected in its leadership of the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting and the ADSSR initiative.

items.title: Wan Saiful urges Putrajaya to consider shutting pig farms, says imported pork ‘safer’, may be cheaper
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — Opposition lawmaker Wan Saiful Wan Jan today urged the federal government to consider shutting down pig farms nationwide, as Putrajaya reviews the industry chain. “Personally, I feel it would not be excessive for me to propose that the federal government consider whether it is appropriate for Malaysia to continue having large pig farms when pork supplies can be obtained through imports, as done in Singapore. Wan Saiful added that pig farming in Malaysia was likely to face opposition from local residents regardless of location, describing Singapore’s reliance on imports as a “safer” approach.

items.title: Deputy minister: No payment delays affecting Pan Borneo Highway project
items.summary: “Phase 1A, comprising 15 work packages, had achieved 89.54 per cent physical completion against a scheduled 96.23 per cent, while financial disbursements stood at 88.78 per cent. “For Phase 1B, which has only recently begun, actual physical progress stands at 25.53 per cent, ahead of the scheduled 24.76 per cent. “Financial disbursements have reached 22.11 per cent, exceeding the scheduled 20.73 per cent.

items.title: Court of Appeal revives 1MDB bid to challenge US$3.7b judgment against Jho Low and father
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — The Court of Appeal today gave 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and four of its subsidiaries another chance to challenge a High Court ruling that ordered fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and his father, Larry Low Hock Peng, to pay more than US$3.7 billion. According to Free Malaysia Today (FMT), the three member bench, chaired by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli, directed that the application be heard afresh before a different High Court judge. Neither Jho Low nor his father was present or represented in court.

items.title: PAC launches probe into Sabah Pan Borneo Highway after audit reveals delays despite RM10.5b spent
items.summary: PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said that from 2016 to March 31, 2026, RM10.547 billion, or 94.6 per cent of the RM11.153 billion allocation, had been spent, although the project’s physical progress was far behind schedule. She disclosed that the 706-kilometre (km) project, comprising 35 work packages, was expected to be fully completed by the end of 2021, but only four work packages, or 11.4 per cent, had been completed. “While the remaining 31 work packages, worth RM16.319 billion, are still being implemented, the project should have been completed five years ago.

items.title: Finance Ministry staff urged to use ‘ATM’ approach to fast-track Budget 2027
items.summary: The event was officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister. He said MoF would also draft a State-Owned Enterprises Act to strengthen governance in the investment and procurement activities of government-owned entities, including statutory bodies and companies under Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc). “On governance, the Prime Minister also announced that MoF would draft a State-Owned Enterprises Act to strengthen governance, particularly in investment and procurement by government-owned entities, including statutory bodies and MOF Inc companies.

items.title: On loan to Japan, welfare row over Dara, Amoi and Kelat flares up again as Taiping council holds off on latest claims
items.summary: Dara, Amoi and Kelat have lived at Tennoji Zoo in Osaka since March under a 25-year cooperation deal with Taiping Zoo & Night Safari. She said such behaviour calls for a professional assessment of the elephants’ psychological health, Berita Harian reported today. Her group has had two staff at Tennoji Zoo since April, recording the elephants’ behaviour daily.

items.title: Ten‑minute war of words in Dewan Rakyat over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Proceedings in the Dewan Rakyat turned heated today after a war of words broke out between government and opposition MPs over the use of the term “munafik”, allegedly directed at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. According to Berita Harian (BH), the exchange, which lasted nearly 10 minutes, began when RSN Rayer (PH–Jelutong) raised Standing Order 36(1), claiming that Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN–Kota Bharu) had used the word while debating the Supply Bill 2027. Rayer questioned why Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng had allowed Takiyuddin to continue without intervening.

items.title: Papagomo walks free after acquittal on sedition charge over Facebook remarks
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, was acquitted and discharged by the Klang Sessions Court today of a sedition charge over remarks allegedly made on Facebook three years ago. His lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said Judge Siti Aminah Ghazali delivered the decision at the conclusion of the defence case. He said only Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, testified for the defence, while Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Mustaffa P. Kunyalam prosecuted the case.

items.title: Roland Sagah says 680 Sarawak schools unsafe, calls for urgent upgrades
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 19 — A total of 680 schools in Sarawak have been classified as unsafe for occupancy, highlighting the scale of infrastructure upgrading needed across the state, said Datuk Seri Roland Sagah Wee Inn. The Education, Innovation and Talent Development Minister said the schools were categorised under Scale 6 and 7, indicating the need for substantial investment in upgrading and improvement works. Sagah also expressed appreciation to the federal government for allocating RM1.3 billion under Budget 2027 to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools nationwide, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: Which book says 1MDB debts are all paid? Anwar wants to know
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims that all 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) debts have been paid. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government is still footing the bill, interest included, The New Straits Times reported. The Finance Ministry has put the government’s total 1MDB-related obligations at RM51.4 billion, of which RM42.5 billion has been paid and RM8.9 billion remains outstanding.

items.title: Sarawak infectious disease centre 90pc complete, set for launch in 2027
items.summary: Sarawak Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Seri Roland Sagah Wee Inn said the RM320 million facility would support disease surveillance and research into infectious diseases. He said SIDC’s Disease Surveillance Programme (DSP) had conducted 13 exercises across southern Sarawak, involving more than 1,000 participants. Meanwhile, Sagah said Sarawak would host the World Robot Olympiad (WRO) Open Championship in 2027.

items.title: Penang secures RM33.22b for 280 federal development projects
items.summary: In a statement today, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the projects comprise 44 new projects and 236 ongoing projects, with RM2.68 billion allocated for implementation in 2027. The 44 new projects have a combined cost of RM578.29 million, with RM63.71 million allocated for next year, he said. Of these, four state priority projects submitted by the Penang state government in February have also been approved, Chow said.

items.title: Selangor Palace seeks investigation into alleged fake Raja Muda bodyguard
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — The Selangor Palace has expressed serious concern over allegations that an individual had impersonated the Raja Muda of Selangor’s personal bodyguard to deceive members of the public for financial gain. In a statement, the Office of the Sultan of Selangor said it had received reports concerning the alleged impersonation, which involved purported deals for land and luxury cars. “The Selangor Palace administration takes this matter seriously and has referred it to the Royal Malaysia Police for a thorough, fair and transparent investigation.

items.title: Zahid tells Negri Sembilan representatives to put public welfare first
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has advised the coalition’s 18 Negeri Sembilan state assemblymen to stay out of matters involving customary law and the royal institution, and instead focus on the people’s welfare and fulfilling their mandate. The Deputy Prime Minister said matters concerning customary law and royal institutions should be kept separate from the administration of the state government to ensure that public services were not disrupted. Ahmad Zahid said the Negeri Sembilan government was preparing a draft of the state’s 2027 Budget despite not having a full state executive council (Exco) line-up at present.

items.title: Dr Mahathir thanks Malaysians for support after Hasmah’s passing, says strength has yet to fully return
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today thanked Malaysians for their support, prayers and assistance following the death and burial of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali, while acknowledging that he has yet to fully regain his strength. In a Facebook post today, Dr Mahathir said he had attempted to return to his office over the past few days but remained physically weak. “Over the last day or two, I tried going to the office but my strength has not yet fully returned,” he said.

items.title: PM Anwar says subsidy rationalisation toughest act, but vital to curb wastage
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Subsidy rationalisation is one of the toughest economic acts but it is necessary to plug wastages and leakages in Malaysia, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said even his predecessors such as Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Datuk Seri Najib Razak had attempted the measure but lacked the determination to implement it. Anwar said his administration has also increased cash aid allocations under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM15 billion, up from the RM8 billion earmarked by the previous administration.

items.title: DKU hauls Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim, 16 others to court over throne dispute
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 19 — The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin have gone to court seeking permission to start contempt proceedings against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, 10 former state executive councillors and six others. The application, filed at the Seremban High Court on Oct 15, names 17 individuals. They include the menteri besar, the former exco members whose appointments were revoked in September, and six plaintiffs in an ongoing case.

items.title: ECRL fares start at RM60 for Gombak-Kuantan route, RM125 one-way to Kota Bharu
items.summary: GOMBAK, Oct 19 — Fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) will start from as low as RM60 one way for Economy Transit services between Gombak and Kota Sultan Ahmad Shah (KotaSAS) in Kuantan, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said today. Economy Transit tickets for the 523km Gombak-Kota Bharu route will start at RM125 one way, while Express fares will start at RM147. Fares for the 378km Gombak-Kuala Terengganu route will start at RM95 for Transit and RM110 for Express.
